paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God cares about the inside. The Pharisees kept the outside of the cup spotless, but Jesus says that inside they are "full of greed and wickedness" (Luke 11:39). And then He asks, "Did not the One who made the outside make the inside as well?" (Luke 11:40). A shiny lid on the cookie box means NOTHING if nobody checks the dough.

Look at what Jesus actually goes after. They tithed mint, rue and every herb, but they disregarded "justice and the love of God" (Luke 11:42). They loved the chief seats and the greetings (Luke 11:43). The experts in the law piled heavy burdens on people and wouldn't lift a finger to help (Luke 11:46), and they took away the key to knowledge (Luke 11:52). Jesus never says drop the small stuff, either. He says to practice justice and the love of God "without neglecting the former" (Luke 11:42). Friend, God wants the whole heart, and the herbs too.

So here's my question for you, baker: what's in YOUR cup? I ask myself that, because I know how easy it is to polish the outside and hope nobody looks. Jesus isn't asking us to look impressive. He's asking us to be real, to love people, to treat them fairly and to help carry the load. And this teaching isn't over, because the scribes and Pharisees are already waiting to catch Him in His words (Luke 11:53-54).
